items.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
items.author: Adam Satariano and Paul Mozur
items.content: <article>Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.</article>

items.title: The Generation That’s Never Had to Say ‘Hello?’
items.author: Alisha Haridasani Gupta
items.content: <article>Now that there’s rarely any mystery to who’s calling, Gen Z has adopted a range of custom phone greetings — including no greeting at all.</article>

items.title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
items.author: Neil Vigdor
items.content: <article>The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.</article>

items.title: Court Filings In A.I. Suit Invoke Copyright Law, Culture and Sports
items.author: Mike Isaac and Karen Weise
items.content: <article>Filings made Friday in The New York Times’s closely watched lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft included a range of copyright law and cultural references.</article>

items.title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
items.author: Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.</article>

items.title: F.B.I. Investigates Sale of Millions of Stolen Driver’s Licenses
items.author: Christine Hauser
items.content: <article>The blog Krebs on Security reported on an identity theft service trying to sell scans of licenses and other documents belonging to people in Canada and the United States.</article>

items.title: Tesla’s Cybercab Is Being Investigated by Federal Regulators
items.author: Jack Ewing
items.content: <article>The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it would examine whether the company’s new self-driving taxi, which has no steering wheel, meets federal auto regulations.</article>

items.title: Tumbler Ridge Shooting Survivors File 30 Lawsuits Against OpenAI
items.author: Michael Levenson
items.content: <article>The survivors contend that the company should have notified the police when it shut down the shooter’s disturbing ChatGPT account eight months before the February attack in British Columbia.</article>

items.title: Why the Hugging Face Hack Should Make You Worry More About A.I.
items.author: Kevin Roose
items.content: <article>The attack by an aggressive “collective” of OpenAI agents shows the danger of artificial intelligence systems that organize themselves.</article>

items.title: How OpenAI Limited the Probe of Its Bots’ Hack of Hugging Face
items.author: Dylan Freedman
items.content: <article>Researchers investigating how OpenAI’s A.I. agents were able to break into Hugging Face’s infrastructure weren’t allowed to look at the incident’s full scope.</article>

items.title: Corporate America Is Getting Hooked on Open-Source A.I.
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Companies like AT&T are increasingly using cheap, freely available artificial intelligence models over expensive ones from Anthropic and OpenAI.</article>

items.title: The A.I. Mob That Attacked Hugging Face + METR’s Ajeya Cotra
items.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Whitney Jones, Davis Land, Vjeran Pavic, Chris Wood, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Diane Wong
items.content: <article>This is probably the most important thing to have happened in A.I. this year.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal
items.author: Kalley Huang, Lauren Hirsch and Kate Conger
items.content: <article>The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.</article>

items.title: Noise and Motion Monitors in Their Homes? These Tenants Say No.
items.author: Kashmir Hill
items.content: <article>The public housing authority in Concord, N.H., installed monitoring devices in 300 homes. Tenants are now suing to remove the Minut sensors.</article>

items.title: In a Big Win, Google Won’t Have to Break Up Its Ad Tech Business, Court Rules
items.author: David McCabe and Tripp Mickle
items.content: <article>In a long-awaited decision, a federal judge said Google must change its ad tech business to address antitrust issues, but did not disclose the measures.</article>

items.title: Justice Dept. Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Suit
items.author: Karen Weise and Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>The department argued in a court filing that OpenAI legally used articles by The New York Times to develop A.I., adding that national security depended on American tech dominance.</article>

items.title: Uber Lays Off 10% of Employees in Sweeping Reorganization
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The layoffs affect about 3,300 workers, as Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi bets on a “leaner organization.”</article>

items.title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
items.author: Alex Williams
items.content: <article>He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.</article>

items.title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
items.author: J. D. Biersdorfer
items.content: <article>In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.</article>

items.title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
items.author: David McCabe and Lauren McCarthy
items.content: <article>Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.</article>

items.title: Map Apps Are Handling Trump’s Renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America Differently
items.author: Victor Mather
items.content: <article>Navigation companies face a new dilemma after President Trump ordered Lake Ontario to be renamed Lake America.</article>

items.title: John Ternus Replaces Tim Cook as Apple CEO
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>Big technology and management changes are greeting John Ternus, whose long-serving predecessor, Tim Cook, will stay on as executive chair.</article>

items.title: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Advertising Practices
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>Regulators say the e-commerce giant forced more than a million advertisers to pay more than they should have. The company denies the claims.</article>
